Proceedings in this case have arisen out of filing of Dar in Fir No.385/2017 of Ps Vivek Vihar
under Section 279/338 Ipc. Perusal Mact No.661/2017 Shelender Shelender Malik Page 1

MALIK Date: 2024.10.09 16:22:41 +0530 of record shows that on 09.08.2017 injured/claimant Tikam Singh was going towards Yojna Vihar on foot, when he reached in front of Gate No.3, one motorcycle bearing registration no.UP-27AG-7339 suddenly came from behind, being driven in a rash and negligent manner and at very high speed, hit the petitioner with a great force due to which he sustained injuries.
On the call police reached at the spot and took the injured to Dr.Hedgewar Hospital where he remained admitted in hospital for his medical treatment.
2. Initially FIR was registered on the call regarding the accident.

Later statement of injured during the investigation was recorded and on the basis of information received regarding vehicle involved Tikam Singh vs Mohd Ali on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181861383/
1 in the accident i.e. motorcycle bearing registration no.UP-27AG-7339
, IO served a notice under Section 133 of M.V. Act and thereupon respondent no.1/driver of the offending vehicle appeared before IO and was arrested and later released on police bail.
It appeared from the investigation that at the time of accident the driver/respondent no.1 was holding learner's licence.
After completion of investigation charge sheet was filed and DAR was filed before this Tribunal.
3. Since the filing of DAR repeatedly notices were issued to respondent no.1 and as per the orders of ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal, counsel for respondent no.1 and 2 put appearance on 22.01.2021.
However WS was not filed.
In the meantime respondent no.1 stated to have expired.
Fact remains that WS has never been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2 despite having notice of the matter.
4. WS on behalf of respondent no.3 has been filed taking an objection that driver of the offending vehicle no.UP-27AG-7339 was not having valid DL at the time of accident.
As such there has been a breach of MACT No.661/2017 Digitally signed by SHELENDER Page 2 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.09 16:22:49 +0530 terms of insurance policy.
Consequently respondent no.3 denied the liability to pay the compensation.
It is stated that insurance company takes all the legal pleas as available under Section 134(c), 147, 149 of M.V. Act.
On merits it is not disputed that vehicle/motorcycle no.UP-27AG-7339 was insured with respondent no.3 in the name of Khurshid Alam/respondent no.2.
However other averments have been denied.

5. During the course of proceedings medical condition of the petitioner was assessed by the medical board of GTB Hospital and found permanent disability to the extent of 6% in relation to left shoulder.
6. Unfortunately issues in this case have not been framed.

However fact remains that basic issue for deciding the claim petition/DAR is following :
"Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 09.08.2017 at 1858 hours at Yamuna Sports Complex Gate No.3, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing No.UP-27AG-7339 being driven by respondent no.1/driver?
If so whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so to what extent and from whom?
7. During the course of proceedings petitioner Tikam Singh has been examined as PW1.
On behalf of insurance company one witness Ms.Ankita (R3W1) was examined.
8. I have heard Sh.Subhash Chand, ld. Counsel for petitioner as well as Sh.Rajesh Goel, ld. counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company.
I have also gone through written submissions filed on behalf of petitioner.
Issue regarding suffering injuries by petitioner due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 9.

It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the MACT No.661/2017 Digitally signed by SHELENDER Page 3 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.09 16:22:55 +0530 principle Tikam Singh vs Mohd Ali on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181861383/
2
of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: In order to prove the manner in which accident has taken place, injured/petitioner Tikam Singh (PW1) in his affidavit of examination in chief has testified that on 09.08.2017 he was going towards Yogna Vihar red light in front of gate no.3 on foot, suddenly a motorcycle bearing no.UP-27AG-7339 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and at high speed and hit the petitioner with great force due to which he sustained injuries all over his body.
PW1 says that someone called the police, police came at the spot and took him to Dr.Hedgewar Hospital where he remained admitted for few days and he is still under treatment.
11. Nothing substantive came in the cross examination of PW1 to disbelieve his testimony regarding the manner in which accident has taken place.

Moreover petitioner in his cross examination stated that at the time of accident he was standing on the cut of Shreshta Vihar just before the red light signal when offending vehicle came from front in the wrong direction of traffic flow.
PW1 says that the motorcyclist was not having any pillion
MACT No.661/2017 SHELENDER Page 4 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.09 16:23:02 +0530 rider.
Witness says that he tried to save himself but the motorcyclist followed and hit him.

Evidence of petitioner has been duly corroborated from documents annexed with the DAR Ex.PW1/3 (colly.) i.e. copy of FIR, MLC of injured, site plan of the place of accident, mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, seizure memo of offending motorcycle from the place of accident, etc.

Thus from the testimony of petitioner/ injured (PW1)
coupled with documents placed on record, it is established by preponderance of probability that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving offending vehicle no.UP-27AG-7339.
Issue accordingly stands decided.
Issue regarding compensation 12.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd. 1995 AIR 755.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd. 1995 AIR 755
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned,
Tikam Singh vs Mohd Ali on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181861383/
3

sentences.text:
they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of MACT No.661/2017 Page 5 SHELENDER by SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
2024.10.09 16:23:08 +0530 injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit;
(iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort,
disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
13. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:

Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
 (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the MACT No.661/2017 SHELENDER  MALIK Date: 2024.10.09  16:23:14 +0530 injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
Tikam Singh vs Mohd Ali on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181861383/
4
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

14. In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses 15.
PW1/petitioner though has been examined, however in his entire evidence no document has been proved regarding medical expenses.
Admittedly petitioner had taken entire treatment in Dr.Hedgewar Hospital which is a government hospital.

It is matter of record that no medical treatment record has been placed on record but on record there is a disability certificate showing 6%
permanent disability to the petitioner.

As MACT No.661/2017 SHELENDER MALIK Page 7 MALIK Date:
2024.10.09 16:23:20 +0530 such considering the overall nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner in the accident, notional amount of Rs.10,000/- in lump sum is fixed towards medical expenses.
Loss of earning during treatment 16.
Petitioner in his deposition stated that at the time of accident he was doing a private job and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
However petitioner has not led any evidence regarding his job or regarding his income of Rs.25,000/- per month as claimed.

In the absence of same, this Tribunal would have to assess the notional income of the petitioner at parity with minimum wages of Tikam Singh vs Mohd Ali on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181861383/
5 unskilled worker prevalent in Delhi which at the time of accident was Rs.13,584/- per month.
17.
Now the question is period of treatment.
Considering the nature of injuries as reflected from medical documents annexed with DAR, disability certificate, petitioner must have gone under medical treatment for period of two months.
As such petitioner is entitled for loss of income of Rs.27,168/- (Rs.13,584 X 02 months).
Loss of future earning due to disability 18.

In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:-
"9.
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.
If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively Tikam Singh vs Mohd Ali on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181861383/
6 carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."
....If doctor has given evidence about percentage of MACT No.661/2017 by SHELENDER Page 9 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.09 16:23:36 +0530 permanent disability

, Tribunal will have to seek doctors opinion as to whether it is possible to deduce the corresponding functional permanent disability with reference to whole body and if so to what percentage.
13.

We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i). All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
(ii). The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability).

(iii). The doctor who treated an injured- claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv). The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession,
occupation or job, age, education and other factors."
19.

Keeping in view the ratio as discussed above, in the present case it is evident on record that as a result of the injuries sustained by petitioner in an accident, he suffered 6% permanent disability in relation to left shoulder.

In this regard it is worthwhile to mention that petitioner was MACT No.661/2017 SHELENDER by SHELENDER Page 10 MALIK Date: 2024.10.09 16:23:42 +0530 referred to medical board of GTB Hospital for assessment of his medical disability and the medical board issued disability certificate no.1209/24/11/2023 dated 16.11.2023 Ex.PW1/2, issued to petitioner/ injured Tikam Singh.

The disablement and loss of earning capacity are two different aspects and may not corresponding to each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of accident.

As per case of petitioner,
he was working in a bangle factory.
It came in the evidence of petitioner that due to accidental injury his working capacity stated to have affected adversely as he could not work properly due to accidental injuries.

sentences.text: In Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (supra) Hon'ble Apex Court in para 11 and 12 has observed that Tribunal should not be a silent spectator when medical evidence is tendered regarding injuries.

Tribunal is required to hold inquiry into the claim for determining just compensation by assessing the medical permanent disability as well as functional disability keeping in view nature of work,
profession etc. of the injured.
The percentage of permanent disability of whole body cannot be presumed to be percentage loss of earning.
Therefore Tribunal is bound to assess corresponding functional disability to compute the future loss of income.

21. Having considered the material annexed with DAR, MLC of petitioner and disability certificate reflect that petitioner suffered permanent disability to the extent of 6% in relation to left shoulder.

As such this Tribunal finds that the functional disability to whole body of the petitioner to be half of his medical disability i.e. 3%.
22.
Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr. (2017) 3 SCC 351].

entities.text: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr. (2017) 3 SCC 351

sentences.text: In his evidence petitioner/injured MACT No.661/2017 by SHELENDER Page 11 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.09 16:23:49 +0530 (PW1) proved his Aadhar card as Ex.PW1/1, as per which his date of birth is mentioned to be 01.01.1952.
Accident in the present case occurred on 09.08.2017.
There is no dispute with regard to age of the petitioner.
Thus age of the petitioner at the time of accident is taken to be 66 years.

As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 5 as applicable to age group between 61-65 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.

Keeping in view the ratio of judgments in Sandeep Khanuja (supra) and Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd. 2020 SCC OnLine SC 601,
since the petitioner is above 60 years of age, therefore he is not entitled for any benefit of loss of future prospects.

sentences.text: 23. As discussed above, the income of petitioner has been assessed as Rs.13,584 and while applying the functional disability to be 3% of Rs.13,584/-, amount comes out to be Rs.408/-.
As such the loss of future earning due to disability comes out to be Rs.408 X 12 X 5 = Rs.24,480/-.

Special Diet &
Conveyance Charges 24.

Though petitioner in his evidence has testified that he spent Rs.30,000/- each on special diet and conveyance during the course of treatment, however fact remains that no documentary evidence or mateiral has been placed on judicial record to substantiate such fact.

In the absence of any evidence or prescription of doctor showing prescribing of any special diet, conveyance charges or any evidence to show that any expenditure has been incurred under the above said heading, this Tribunal grants compensation on lump sum basis of Rs.10,000/- each on the heads of special diet and conveyance charges.
Attendant Charges 25.

Though no specific evidence has been led by the petitioner MACT No.661/2017 by SHELENDER Page 12 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.09 16:23:56 +0530 with regard to engaging any attendant for taking care of him, however in his affidavit petitioner testified that he spent Tikam Singh vs Mohd Ali on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181861383/
8 Rs.30,000/- on attendant.
In view of MLC and permanent disability certificate of the petitioner, this Tribunal assesses the charges for attendant on lump sum basis of Rs.10,000/- under the above said head.

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Pain & Sufferings 26.

While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No:
709/02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered:
"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objectives co-relation with the pain and suffering.

13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."
27.
In this case, as per MLC and other material placed on record, petitioner received injuries on his left side of head with pain and tenderness over left clavicular region.
Such injuries were opined by the doctor to be grievous in nature.
It is also matter of record that petitioner also suffered permanent disability on his left shoulder.

Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.25,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
MACT No.661/2017

MALIK Date: 2024.10.09
Accordingly, Rs.25,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
Loss of Amenities 28.

It is evident on record that even after completion of treatment, petitioner sustained 6%
permanent physical disability in relation to left shoulder which has been assessed as 3% functional Tikam Singh vs Mohd Ali on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181861383/
9 disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner by this Tribunal.
It cannot be ignored that with the aforementioned disability, petitioner is bound to face difficulties throughout his life and will not be able to enjoy the amenities of life to the fullest.
In view of this, the petitioner is granted a compensation of Rs.15,000/- under this head.

29. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-

 treatment  3. Loss of Future Earnings Rs.24,480/-

LIABILITY 32.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.

Respondent no.3/insurance company has led the evidence of R3W1 Ms.Ankita, Assistant Manager who has testified that vehicle in question though was insured with it, however driver and owner of the offending vehicle were served with notice under Order 12 rule 8 CPC for producing original DL,
insurance policy and other documents.
However despite service of that notice DL was not furnished.

Moreover it came in the investigation itself that driver Mohd. Ali was not having valid DL at the time of accident and was holding only learner's licence and driver was not accompanied with any licenced person as required under Central Motor Vehicle Rules.
33. R3W1 was not cross-examined at all on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2.

In view of evidence of R3W1 as well as report of IO being part of DAR, it is established that record by preponderance of probability that respondent no.1/driver was only holding learner's driving licence and was not accompanied with any other person with valid DL.
Therefore there was breach of insurance policy.

However fact remains that basic issue for deciding the claim petition/DAR is following :
"Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 09.08.2017 at 1858 hours at Yamuna Sports Complex Gate No.3, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing No.UP-27AG-7339 being driven by respondent no.1/driver?
If so whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so to what extent and from whom?
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.
After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively Tikam Singh vs Mohd Ali on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181861383/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
10.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd. 1995 AIR 755.
The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
Considering the nature of injuries as reflected from medical documents annexed with DAR, disability certificate, petitioner must have gone under medical treatment for period of two months.
As such petitioner is entitled for loss of income of Rs.27,168/- (Rs.13,584 X 02 months).
The disablement and loss of earning capacity are two different aspects and may not corresponding to each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of accident.
Tikam Singh vs Mohd Ali on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181861383/
7 20.
In Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (supra) Hon'ble Apex Court in para 11 and 12 has observed that Tribunal should not be a silent spectator when medical evidence is tendered regarding injuries.
Tribunal is required to hold inquiry into the claim for determining just compensation by assessing the medical permanent disability as well as functional disability keeping in view nature of work,
profession etc. of the injured.
The percentage of permanent disability of whole body cannot be presumed to be percentage loss of earning.
Therefore Tribunal is bound to assess corresponding functional disability to compute the future loss of income.
21. Having considered the material annexed with DAR, MLC of petitioner and disability certificate reflect that petitioner suffered permanent disability to the extent of 6% in relation to left shoulder.
As such this Tribunal finds that the functional disability to whole body of the petitioner to be half of his medical disability i.e. 3%.
22.
Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr. (2017) 3 SCC 351].
Thus age of the petitioner at the time of accident is taken to be 66 years.
As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 5 as applicable to age group between 61-65 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.
Thus, it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, I am of the opinion that an amount of Rs.25,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
Moreover it came in the investigation itself that driver Mohd. Ali was not having valid DL at the time of accident and was holding only learner's licence and driver was not accompanied with any licenced person as required under Central Motor Vehicle Rules.
33. R3W1 was not cross-examined at all on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2.
In view of evidence of R3W1 as well as report of IO being part of DAR, it is established that record by preponderance of probability that respondent no.1/driver was only holding learner's driving licence and was not accompanied with any other person with valid DL.
Therefore there was breach of insurance policy.
